QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_9

question.text: Fund monitoring for a Cat III AIF is BEST described as:

answer.text: Day-to-day investment decision-making by the LPs
An oversight process on asset allocation, portfolio composition, fund governance and performance
The same activity as fund management — terms are interchangeable
A discretionary marketing exercise done only at fund launch

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 13.1.1 positions fund monitoring as an OVERSIGHT process over asset allocation, portfolio composition, fund governance and performance — NOT the same as fund management, where investors have no involvement. Monitoring is ongoing; it is neither day-to-day management nor a one-off launch activity. The Trap: Option A confuses monitoring with management. Option C conflates both — the PDF explicitly separates them. Option D trivialises it to marketing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A / XIX-B (distributor exams) test the client-facing view of monitoring reports. XIX-D/E test the manager-side execution. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a monitoring dashboard the IC can read in 10 minutes: NAV, MTD/YTD/ITD return, Sharpe, gross/net exposure, top-5 longs/shorts, VaR vs limit, margin utilisation vs 2x cap, redemption queue, exception log. That IS fund monitoring in practice.
